newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money firm, steady in cautious market.
newsitem.headline: German call money firm, steady in cautious market.

text.p: German call money rates held steady in calm trade on Tuesday, narrowing the range to around 3.07 to 3.08 percent from 3.06 to 3.09 percent on Monday.

Dealers said rates were still relatively firm for the beginning of the month because of some lingering fears in the market after rates jumped unexpectedly late in June and forced banks to borrow heavily from the Lombard emergency facility.
"The market is being over cautious because rates at the end of last month were so high," said one Frankfurt-based trader.
"At this point last month no-one was even thinking about reserve levels."
Another trader said that by keeping rates relatively firm, the market wanted to signal to the Bundesbank that there were concerns about liquidity levels.
Market particpiants said they expected the Bundesbank to add some liquidity to the market with its repurchase agreement operation on Wednesday, when 69.6 billion marks in two-week repos will expire.

Central banks held daily reserves of 39.8 billion marks at the Bundesbank on Monday, unchanged from Friday's levels, while the monthly average reserve level eased down to 41.1 billion marks from 41.3 billion on Friday.
Borrowing on the Lombard facility, which on Friday reached 100 million marks, was negligible on Monday, Bundesbank data showed.
On Tuesday, the Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA rate was quoted at 3.10000 percent versus 3.10467 percent on Monday.
